practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(GraphTest.class), providing categorization for selective execution which satisfies labeling best practices.

The test verifies two distinct behaviors: that numVertices() returns the configured size AND that no self-loop exists for vertex 0. There are effectively two 'Act' checks/assertion groups in one method, violating atomicity.

The method creates its own Grafo instance as a local variable and does not modify shared mutable state in the method body. No evidence of relying on other tests or global mutable state is present in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a happy-path check is present; there is no test of error conditions or exception handling for invalid inputs (no assertThrows/@Test(expected=...) or try-catch validating exceptions).
The test explicitly checks vertex 0 for absence of a self-loop, which represents a boundary (zero) case; this indicates attention to boundary values within the test.
The test uses named constants (SIZE_OTHER, VERTEX_ZERO) instead of inline magic numbers and is short and self-contained; there is no evident duplication within this single method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is concise (well under 20 lines), linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals, satisfying low complexity guidelines.
The test contains multiple specific assertions (two checks) that verify different properties of the Grafo instance rather than a single superficial assertion, improving fault-detection capability.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present in the method. Comments are active explanatory comments, so the test appears active and runnable.
There is no annotation or Javadoc in the method linking the test to a requirement ID, ticket, or user story; comments mention intent but do not reference a concrete requirement identifier.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method includes a timeout in the @Test annotation (timeout = 4000), which is an explicit performance-related constraint, satisfying the presence of performance checks.
The method name 'test7' is generic and does not describe the scenario or the expected behavior, violating descriptive naming conventions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: No signs of code-generation artifacts (auto-generated comments or repetitive auto names) are present in the method; the practice is not applicable to this single, handcrafted test method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The method includes Given/When/Then comments, indicating BDD-style organization and deliberate design intent for the test scenario.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts with the public Grafo API and does not access private fields or use reflection; assertions are based on observable behavior rather than implementation internals.
Assertions include descriptive failure messages and use specific assertion methods (assertEquals, assertFalse), improving clarity and diagnostic value.
Comments follow Given/When/Then and explain intent rather than stating obvious code mechanics; there are no commented-out code blocks, and comments are minimal and purposeful.
No sources of non-determinism (Random, current time, Thread.sleep, or external calls) are used within the method; the test uses a fresh local Grafo instance and deterministic assertions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses local objects and does not persist data or modify global/static state within the method; no cleanup is required for resources created only inside the test.
